note: Cumulative toll as of early August 2026 across the Gironde, Aude-Hérault and other French fire fronts.
Includes 2 firefighting helicopter crew killed in a mid-air collision near Psatha (2 August) and 2 killed in the Salamis Island fires (16 August).

By 4 August 2026 fires had killed at least 17 civilians, 6 firefighters and 2 helicopter crew across Spain and France combined, per AP tally at that date; later national counts (Spain 16, France 25) reflect subsequent deaths.
France's national public health agency said deaths during the late-June heatwave were 36% above the anticipated baseline — the highest mortality rate recorded since the 2003 heatwave.
WHO's attributed count for the June heatwave (327) is far below independent modelled excess-mortality estimates for the same period; totals continue to be revised as more data comes in.
Over 70% of the late-June/early-July fatalities occurred among people aged 85 and older.
Over a dozen major Italian cities issued consecutive red heatwave alerts and reported significant excess mortality among the elderly, but no single confirmed national death count has been published.

Modelled excess-mortality estimate for a single week is an order of magnitude above WHO's confirmed-attributed figure of 1,300+ for the same period — reflects the gap between statistical excess-mortality modelling and officially attributed heat deaths.

More than 320,000-330,000 people evacuated across Spain and France combined as of late July/early August 2026 — includes 220,000+ in Gironde, 60,000 in Ávila/Madrid, 30,000 in Landes, 18,000 in Castellón.
More than 10,000 residents and visitors forced to evacuate across Crete, Attica and Boeotia, including ~8,000 from the Rethymno fire alone.
Nineteen people were treated for smoke inhalation in the Castellón (Vall d'Uixó) fire alone; comprehensive region-wide injury counts are not centrally tracked.
